sections.skill: Search for legitimate rental listings and recognize rental scams

questions.prompt: A listing offers a 2-bedroom apartment for $700 a month when similar ones nearby rent for $1,500. The "owner" is overseas and asks for a deposit by wire before anyone sees the unit. What is most likely happening?

choices.text: A rare bargain that should be secured quickly
A normal practice for overseas landlords
A rental scam
A government housing program

questions.intro: Rental scammers copy real listings or invent fake ones. Red flags: rent far below similar units, an owner who cannot meet in person, pressure to pay quickly, requests to wire money or use gift cards or payment apps, and requests for payment before you see the unit or sign a lease.
questions.feedback: Below-market rent, an absent owner, and a wire request before viewing are classic scam signs.
questions.topic: Finding a rental and avoiding rental scams
sources: FTC: Rental listing scams include fake listings, requests to wire money or pay before seeing a unit, and owners who claim to be out of the country. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/rental-listing-scams)

questions.prompt: Which step BEST confirms that a listing is real before paying anything?

choices.text: Visit the unit in person and verify the owner or manager
Ask the poster to send more photos of the unit before deciding
Pay a small deposit to hold it
Trust the listing because it is on a big website

questions.correct_answer: Visit the unit in person and verify the owner or manager
questions.intro: Before paying, see the unit in person (or have someone you trust visit), meet the landlord or property manager, and check who owns the property, for example through local property records.
questions.feedback: In-person viewing and verifying the owner prevent most rental scams.

choices.text: A, by $30

questions.intro: Compare total monthly housing cost, not just rent: rent + utilities + parking + renters insurance + other fees.

questions.prompt: Which payment request is MOST likely a sign of a scam?

choices.text: Paying an application fee with gift cards
Paying first month's rent by check after signing a lease

questions.correct_answer: Paying an application fee with gift cards
questions.feedback: Legitimate landlords do not ask for gift cards; scammers do because they cannot be traced or reversed.

sections.skill: Renting basics: landlords, tenants, and leases
sections.relationship: Students need the basic vocabulary of renting before evaluating listings.

questions.prompt: In a rental, who is the TENANT?

choices.text: The person who owns the building
The person who pays rent to live in the home
The bank that holds the mortgage on the building
The city housing inspector

questions.correct_answer: The person who pays rent to live in the home
questions.intro: A landlord owns (or manages) a rental property. A tenant pays rent to live there. A lease is the contract that sets the terms.
questions.feedback: The tenant pays rent to live in the unit.

questions.prompt: What is a lease?

choices.text: A loan agreement that lets the tenant buy the apartment over time
A receipt for one month's rent
A contract between landlord and tenant setting the rental terms
Renters insurance for the apartment

questions.correct_answer: A contract between landlord and tenant setting the rental terms
questions.intro: A lease is a legal agreement that states the rent, length of the rental, rules, and responsibilities of each side.
questions.feedback: The lease is the rental contract.
questions.topic: Finding a rental and avoiding rental scams

misconceptions.B: Confuses a payment record with a contract
